title: Foundations: Jubilee Songs - The Complete Guide
summary: What Jubilee Songs is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Jubilee Songs songs: Jubilee songs are the oldest Black American choral tradition: spirituals arranged for concert quartets and choirs, sung a cappella with intricate harmonies. The Fisk Jubilee Singers introduced them to the world in the 1870s.

History: The Fisk Jubilee Singers toured America and Europe from 1871, raising funds for Fisk University and making spirituals internationally famous. Their 1909–1916 recordings preserve the original style.

How the songs work: Jubilee Songs favors the keys of F, Bb, Eb, G. Common forms include A cappella verse-chorus with layered entrances; Leader-and-chorus call-and-response. Players should master close harmony with the melody in the tenor (traditional) first, then rhythmic clapping and foot-stomping as percussion. A cappella first; accompaniment optional.

title: Swing Low, Sweet Chariot - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Swing Low, Sweet Chariot, a public-domain Jubilee Songs standard.
body:
Swing Low, Sweet Chariot (Attributed to Wallis Willis, c. 1862. Traditional spiritual. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Chorus:
Swing low, sweet chariot,
Coming for to carry me home;
Swing low, sweet chariot,
Coming for to carry me home.

I looked over Jordan, and what did I see,
Coming for to carry me home;
A band of angels coming after me,
Coming for to carry me home.

If you get there before I do,
Coming for to carry me home;
Tell all my friends I'm coming too,
Coming for to carry me home.

I'm sometimes up and sometimes down,
Coming for to carry me home;
But still my soul feels heavenly bound,
Coming for to carry me home.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Jubilee Songs accompaniment in F using the 'Spiritual I–IV–V' pattern:
F | A# | C7 | F

Technique: close harmony with the melody in the tenor (traditional). A cappella first; accompaniment optional.
